resources.string: I\'m made of sound, so I wiggle when things get loud. I\'ll show you around MuzViz: a player, a visualizer that dances to your music, and a studio that turns it into video.
Swipe or tap Next. Skip a chapter you know, or skip the lot. Tap Show me to jump to the real thing; I\'ll wait with a Resume button. Every chapter lives on in Settings › Tutorials.
The Player has your track, the transport and a live spectrum. Tap the artwork to go full screen, which is where the visuals live.
Open the queue to reorder what\'s next or save it as a playlist. Drop an .lrc file beside a track and its lyrics follow along, line by line.
The quick row holds a sleep timer, shuffle all and an A–B loop. Switch the source to the mic or to another app\'s audio and the visuals react to that instead.
Tracks, albums, artists, folders, playlists, plus a Duplicates tab for tidying up. MuzViz reads what Android already knows about.
Tap a track, get the list
Tapping any track queues everything you\'re looking at, so Next and Previous do what you expect.
Search covers titles, artists, albums and folders. Music on an SD card or in Downloads? Add the folder in Settings › Folders.
Tunnels, fluids, fractals, cymatics, MilkDrop and more. Plenty are free, and every style family lets you try its first one. Pro opens the rest.
A preset is a style plus every control around it. Save yours, morph between them, and share one with a friend as a link.
Auto visuals can switch styles at random, at each section of the song, or smartly to match the music. Sit back.

Customize opens on Macros: six knobs for Energy, Speed, Complexity, Mood, Space and Chaos. Twist one and several controls follow it at once. With Pro, Edit macros lets you choose what each knob turns.
Make it hit on the beat

Events, the next tab, has one-tap reactions such as Kick punch, Snare crack and Drop burst, plus the reaction routes and the Manual, Suggest and Auto style switching. They work in exported videos too.
Every detail, if you want it
Shape, Colour, Motion, FX, Reactivity and Scene hold every control the style can use, and Scene's Layers put a second style on top. Anything off its default shows a Reset.
Randomize, or Surprise on Macros, rolls a new look. Undo and Redo sit beside it, and further down A/B lets you keep two versions and blend between them.
The live view is the visualizer with nothing in the way. The controls fade after a few seconds; tap to bring them back.
Your finger is part of it
One finger sets a point the style builds around, two set an axis, three or more open a swirl. Pinch and twist to zoom and rotate.
Picture-in-picture keeps it playing in a small window. Plug into a TV or monitor and the visuals move to the big screen.
Studio › Render exports the visualizer to your gallery. Free videos are up to 1080p, 30 fps and one minute, with a watermark. Pro goes to 4K and 60 fps, full length.
Loop render makes a clip that ends exactly where it began, ready for a canvas, a story or a stream background.
Studio › Edit is a timeline: clips, keyframes, markers, and an auto-cut that drops a cut on every hit in the music.
Your last style can live on your home screen, reacting to whatever MuzViz is playing. Set it up in Settings › Behavior.
On the charger, Android\'s screen saver can show MuzViz too. Pick it in your phone\'s display settings.
Long-press your home screen, add the MuzViz widget, and play, pause or skip without opening the app.
Pro is a one-time purchase: every style, 4K and 60 fps exports with no watermark, loop render, the Studio editor and the live wallpaper.
Start a free one-hour trial to play with every Pro style and tool before you decide. Anything marked Pro tells you where it is.
Look, Audio, Folders and Behavior hold the rest, including reduced motion and visual safety. Backup saves your presets and settings to a file.
That\'s the tour. Replay any chapter in Settings › Tutorials. Now play something loud and watch me go.
Progress cleared. The tour greets you next launch.
